$schema: self-describing — no external schema; read the _readme fields
_readme: Machine-readable index of every capability this engine ships, verified by actually running each one during this package's consolidation (not just read from source) unless a caveat says otherwise. Use this to answer 'can this engine make X' without reading source code. See USAGE_GUIDE.md for narrative walkthroughs, CONFIGURATION.md for path setup, and each engine's own README.md for full detail. See INTERPRETATION.md for what each figure type's collision/precision guarantees actually are (verified against code, not asserted) and which color/layout conventions are real standards vs. this engine's own house style vs. left to whoever authors the figure. REVERIFIED 2026-08-19 end-to-end: every figure kind below was rendered in ONE real document (examples/capability-gallery.html, 21 figures) built through the ordinary CLI, then measured in a browser — 262 text elements, zero overlaps, zero out-of-box text, in BOTH themes. Four fail-closed gates were deliberately triggered and each refused the build. See PROVENANCE.md 'Session 4' for the five defects that pass found and fixed.

document-engine.purpose: Markdown -> self-contained HTML/JSON(/PDF) documents, with 15 embeddable diagram/chart/map renderers (all reachable via the same sidecar-kind pipeline — verified this session), each carrying an optional reader_question/insight interpretive layer (see INTERPRETATION.md), and a 9-gate leak sanitizer.
document-engine.verifiedWorking: Reverified 2026-08-19: all 15 native kinds + both bridges rendered in one real document via `python3 -m tools.docgen.cli build` (examples/capability-gallery.md -> 21 figures, every one carrying a reader_question/insight pair), plus the bundled sample.md and sample-multi-figure.md. Browser-measured: 0 text overlaps and 0 out-of-box labels across 262 text elements, in dark AND light. Gates proven by deliberate failure, not by reading code. Figure system added 2026-10-10 (OG-250..OG-261): verify with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -t .` and, for behaviour in a browser, `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE_DIR=<dir resolving playwright> python3 -m unittest tools.tests.test_figure_runtime_browser`.

documents.what: A Markdown file with a YAML front-matter header (id/classification/title/...) becomes a self-contained HTML document — inline CSS, dark+light theme toggle, masthead, classification badge, embedded figures, no external asset requests.
formats: pdf (if weasyprint installed, else recorded as skipped)
documents.requires: A DOC_MANIFEST.md registry row matching the document's id-prefix (docs/design/doc-system/DOC_MANIFEST.md — bundled with one example row; see CONFIGURATION.md).

flowchart.what: Animated process-flow diagram, 9 node-glyph shapes, edge routing around nodes, a constant-velocity flow-dot, reduced-motion static fallback.

stateDiagram.what: State machine diagram (states + labeled transitions), static.
stateDiagram.note: Reachable via the standard sidecar kind:"state" (falls through to the same VisualSpec parser as flowchart) — verified this session.

systemMap.note: Reachable via sidecar kind:"system_map" — verified this session.

dependencyGraph.note: Reachable via sidecar kind:"dependency_graph" — verified this session.

sequenceDiagram.what: UML-style sequence diagram — vertical actor lifelines, ordered numbered message arrows. No self-messages (stated limitation).

isometric3d.what: TRUE isometric/axonometric 3D — real (x,y,z) cuboids, fixed deterministic projection, painter's-algorithm depth sort, up to 24 boxes.

layeredWorkflow.what: 2.5D layered cross-plane workflow diagram (isometric-shear view + flat reduced-motion/print fallback in one SVG).
layeredWorkflow.verifiedWorking: Wired into the standard sidecar-kind dispatch this session (was previously NOT reachable via the documented <!-- figure:ID --> pipeline despite being claimed as one of docgen's "11 native figure renderers" — a real gap found by an independent audit and fixed same-session). Built a real test document embedding it with reader_question/insight, screenshotted the correct layered/labeled output.

geoMap.what: Schematic point/route map — real projected (lon,lat) coordinates, 5-continent coarse outline, no network. For orientation, not cartographic accuracy.

choropleth.what: REAL country-boundary world map, value-to-color per country, 5-bucket color-mix() scale (theme-reactive). 177 countries, bundled GeoJSON. NEW this session — verified by rendering a standalone sample AND by a full document build embedding it alongside mermaid+echarts figures (tools/docgen/sample-multi-figure.md).
choropleth.kind: choropleth (sidecar spec, same declarative pattern as every other figure kind)
choropleth.namesReference: geo_map.list_choropleth_country_names() — country names are short/common form (e.g. 'USA' not 'United States of America')

moduleExplorer.what: Zoomable, clickable hierarchy: a squarified treemap per level, an animated camera into a part, a panel (what it is, size, colour state, what it calls, who calls it, the documents about it), a reader that opens a dossier in place, hover arrows, keyboard and reduced-motion support, and a plain nested outline without script or in print. A block, not a picture (no design size).
moduleExplorer.note: At most 700 parts, depth 5, 3000 edges. Spec, layout and markup pinned by tools/tests/test_explorer.py; behaviour by tools/tests/browser/explorer_check.mjs in Chromium (not Firefox, Safari or a screen reader). docs/design/FIGURE_SYSTEM.md section 13.

sankey.what: Value-proportional bezier ribbon flow diagram, column-acyclic, single-accent emphasis.

bar/radar/pie/timeline/heatmap.what: 5 data-series chart types with hard selection rules (zero-baseline bars, >=3-axis radar, <=6-slice pie, point-event timeline (not Gantt), mandatory heatmap legend).
bar/radar/pie/timeline/heatmap.note: For the other ~19 chart types (scatter, bubble, funnel, treemap, sunburst, boxplot, etc.) use chart-engine (below) via the echarts bridge — kind: 'echarts' in a figure spec.
bar/radar/pie/timeline/heatmap.kind: bar | radar | pie | timeline | heatmap (five separate sidecar kind values, one per type)
bar/radar/pie/timeline/heatmap.verifiedWorking: Wired into the standard sidecar-kind dispatch this session (same gap/fix as layeredWorkflow above — these 5 were real, working, tested renderer functions that generator.py never actually called). Built and verified all 5 in one test document with reader_question/insight on each.

echartsCharts.what: Bridges to chart-engine's full ECharts catalog (bar/line/area/scatter/bubble/funnel/tree/treemap/sunburst/boxplot/graph/and more) for figures docgen's own 5 native types don't cover.
echartsCharts.requires: chart-engine's node_modules installed (npm install in tools/visual-engine/)

mermaidDiagrams.what: Bridges to mermaid-engine for flowchart/sequence/class/state/ER/xychart diagrams authored in Mermaid text syntax instead of this engine's own spec JSON shapes.
mermaidDiagrams.requires: mermaid-engine's node_modules installed (npm install in tools/mermaid-engine/)
mermaidDiagrams.verifiedWorking: Built a real document embedding a Mermaid flowchart this session, confirmed theme-reactive (dark AND light both verified via computed CSS) and zero CDN requests.

videoScript.what: Markdown storyboard exporter pairing narration with animation_ref pointers — NOT a visual renderer itself, a script/outline format.
videoScript.note: A LIBRARY function, not a command. `entry` read `video_script.py`, which is the shape of a runnable file, and there is none: nothing in this repository calls the module, no CLI subcommand exposes it, and a host project imports it. An AST import graph over all tracked .py files found it and `fetch_public_fact.py` as the only non-test, non-entry-point modules with no importer; that was recorded as P6-37 in Pass 6 and never actioned. Now proven rather than assumed — tools/tests/test_video_script.py retains 7 counter-examples, including the content_role == 'article' eligibility gate refusing every other role. See OG-120.

figureSystem.what: Every figure is numbered (Fig. N), anchored (fig-<slug>), scoped (its ids and its CSS cannot touch another figure), explained (a reading guide per kind, a key to every numbered circle, a mark table for engine charts) and linked to the text: sections are sec-<slug> targets with a chip per figure, each figure links back to its section, and [[fig:ID]] in prose links to the figure. Figures take the full content width, centred, outer border only.
figureSystem.entry: generator._render_markdown_body (single dispatch through _FIGURE_KINDS); components.figure / components.section; figure_support.scope_svg_ids
refuses: a [[fig:ID]] to a figure the document does not place
a figure whose caption/sidecar disagree (existing sidecar gates)

figureRuntime.what: One inline script per document (only when a figure is present): styled tooltip, click-to-pin (Esc releases), nearest-mark assist, keyboard focus, adjacency/series/legend highlighting for any size of figure. Reads the figures' own attributes; writes two classes and a tooltip's textContent; no dependencies, no network, no eval.
figureRuntime.verifiedBy: tools/tests/browser/figure_runtime_check.mjs via tools/tests/test_figure_runtime_browser.py (headless Chromium; skips with the cause when Playwright is absent)

blueprintJson.what: The machine-readable twin of a rendered document: sections with Markdown source, numbered figures with reading keys and (engine charts) the whole per-mark record, every [[fig:]] reference, and the contains/described-by/references link graph. Generated from the same render pass as the HTML and gated by the same leak-gate.

notImplemented.gantt: docgen's own 'timeline' is single-axis point events, NOT task bars with duration/dependencies. Use chart-engine's ECharts custom-series Gantt recipe instead (see chart-engine.capabilities.ganttViaCustomSeries below) — this is ECharts' own official documented pattern, not a workaround.
notImplemented.orgChart/genericTreeLayout: diagram_graphs.py's node/edge diagrams require every node's (x,y) supplied by the caller — no auto-layout algorithm exists in docgen for a plain edge-list. graphify's graph-view.html DOES have auto-layout (dagMode: top-down tree / radial) — see graph-engine below — but that's for graphify's own node-link JSON, not docgen figures.
notImplemented.erDiagram/classDiagram(native): Not in docgen's own 11 renderers. Available via mermaid-engine (kind: 'mermaid', erDiagram/classDiagram syntax).
notImplemented.swimlane/BPMN-lanes: Identified as a gap during this session's research (no lane/pool primitive in docgen, ECharts, or Mermaid) but NOT built — deferred as a smaller nice-to-have, not one of the explicitly requested categories. A future addition would be a small stdlib-only docgen module in the geo_map.py/isometric3d.py style — no new dependency needed.
notImplemented.vennDiagram: Same status as swimlane — identified, not built. 2-3 circle Venn is closed-form geometry (no dependency needed); >3 sets or true area-proportional layout would need a DOM-shimmed third-party library (venn.js) and wasn't judged worth the complexity for this pass.

chart-engine.entryPoint: node adapters/echarts/cli.mjs render <job.json>  OR  MCP server (mcp/server.mjs, 7 tools)
chart-engine.purpose: Deterministic SSR data-chart rendering — the canonical chart engine docgen's echarts_bridge delegates to.
chart-engine.verifiedWorking: npm test: 30/30 unit tests pass. npm run simulate: 22/22 acceptance simulations pass. Re-run 2026-08-19 after that session's two option-builder fixes (treemap/sunburst items-only fallback; axis-name placement) — still 30/30 + 22/22, with one golden re-baselined and classified in renders/diffs/2026-08-19-axis-name-placement.md. Figure layer added 2026-10-10: goldens re-baselined and classified in renders/diffs/2026-10-10-figure-layer.md; verify with `npm test` and `npm run simulate` in tools/visual-engine.

chartFamilies: graph (node-link, layout locked to circular/preset — never force, for determinism)

exportFormats.svg: Canonical, deterministic, content-sha256-stamped. Build-twice byte-identical (locked by golden-render regression tests).
exportFormats.png: Rasterization of the canonical SVG via @resvg/resvg-js — explicitly a convenience format, never archival.
exportFormats.html: Self-contained interactive HTML, echarts.min.js inlined (no CDN), static SVG fallback for reduced-motion/print.
exportFormats.pdf: Indirect only — embed the canonical SVG into a docgen/weasyprint document. No native PDF export path in chart-engine itself.
exportFormats.json: The AI-only per-figure record <visual_id>.figure.json (schema ultimate-engine/figure/1): id, kind, reader question, summary, how to read, series, legend, EVERY MARK with its value, neighbours and a plain-language description, and provenance. Generated from the live ECharts model, so it cannot disagree with the SVG.

ganttViaCustomSeries.what: ECharts' officially-documented custom series (type:'custom' + renderItem: time axis + category axis + one rect per task) is the standard Gantt recipe. Verified as a real, current, officially-published ECharts pattern during this session's research (not hypothetical) — not yet wired as a docgen preset/kind, but usable directly via a job packet with a custom series.
ganttViaCustomSeries.status: Capability exists in the underlying ECharts engine; no docgen-side preset built yet for it.

figureLayer.what: A pass over the finished SVG that makes a chart safe to inline beside others and makes every mark answer: ECharts' own CSS and class names are removed; ids/url(#)/href are scoped to the figure; ecmeta_* become data-*; every mark gets a <title>, data-id and (graphs/trees/sankey) its neighbours; ONE scoped <style> carries a hover law that never recolours, never fills an open path, never moves a mark and never takes the pointer, plus a no-script adjacency/series/legend fallback for up to 160 marks.

readableInk.what: Label ink chosen from the fill by WCAG contrast (brand near-black or white; pure black/white in the mid-tone band); no label halos; per-cell heat-map ink from the visualMap ramp. Severity and status words keep their reserved colours (Critical red … Low blue … Info green); job.semantic_colors:false opts out.

notImplemented.3dCharts: No echarts-gl dependency. Verified this session via npm registry: echarts-gl@2.1.0's peerDependency pins echarts@^5.1.2, INCOMPATIBLE with the vendored echarts@6.1.0 — upgraded from a prior 'unverified' hedge to a confirmed no. Use docgen's isometric3d.py for genuine 3D architecture/spatial diagrams instead — real 3D projection math, no dependency conflict.
notImplemented.geographicMaps(inChartEngine): No GeoJSON/registerMap plumbing in chart-engine itself. Use docgen's geo_map.py (point/route maps) or the new render_choropleth (real country boundaries) instead — both live in document-engine, not here.
notImplemented.dualAxes: Explicitly refused by ENGINE_ROUTING_POLICY.json policy, not a code limitation.

graph-engine.purpose: Codebase cartography — directory-structure, dependency, pipeline-flow, and coverage graphs, rendered as an interactive force-directed / hierarchical / 3D dashboard.
graph-engine.verifiedWorking: Reverified 2026-08-19: build.mjs run against this engine's own tree (130 nodes) AND against a separate external tree via ENGINE_HOST_ROOT (96 nodes, 29 directories) — read-only, output written only into this engine's own graphify-out/. All 4 layout modes and the fully-local 3D vendor load verified in a previous session; the viewer's only unpkg reference is a comment recording the removed CDN fetch, confirmed 2026-08-19.

structureGraph.what: Directory-level containment tree from `codemap`. Host-agnostic — the tree it maps comes from the standard host-root resolution (ENGINE_HOST_ROOT env var > engine.config.json docSystem.hostRoot > `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` > this engine's own directory), so it can be pointed at any codebase without copying the engine into it. Output always lands in this engine's own graphify-out/ regardless of what was scanned, so the scanned tree is never written to.
structureGraph.entry: build.mjs  (ENGINE_HOST_ROOT=/path/to/repo node tools/graphify/build.mjs to target another tree)

dependencyGraph.what: REAL parsed Python import graph with risky-core (highest in-degree) ranking. Worked example tuned to a src/-rooted Python project — configurable via engine.config.json's graphify.srcRoot.

pipelineGraph.what: Curated stage-flow diagram from external DATA (tools/graphify/pipeline.example.json), not hardcoded — author your own pipeline.json in the same shape and point graphify.pipelineStepsFile at it.

coverageGraph.what: detector<->SWC-class<->tag graph with blind-spot detection. Worked example tuned to one project's detector-plugin shape.

viewerLayouts.hierarchicalTree: Top-down tree layout via dagMode — a feature ALREADY in the vendored 2D library, wired up this session (previously unused). Zero new dependency.
viewerLayouts.3d: Real WebGL 3D via vendor/3d-force-graph.min.js — vendored THIS session (was previously a live, unpinned CDN fetch to unpkg.com that failed silently offline; now fully local, MIT license, ~1.3MB, bundles three.js).

notImplemented.clustering/communityDetection: node 'type' only drives a flat color legend, not a computed grouping/hull/cluster-force layout. No dependency currently provides this.
notImplemented.subgraphFiltering: graph-view.html's search centers/zooms to the first match; no isolate/filter-by-type UI.

vault-graph-engine.status: SPEC + VENDORED LIBRARY ONLY — ZERO CONSUMING IMPLEMENTATION. Do not report this as a working component; it is design material.
vault-graph-engine.purpose: A sibling project's own future in-app credential-vault node-graph UI spec (radial hierarchy layout, per-kind node radius table, lock/2FA/grant overlay glyphs, mandatory accessible tree-view mirror) — this is that product's specific UI chrome, not a generic engine capability.
whatExists: force-graph.min.js (vendored, MIT, same file as graph-engine's copy, byte-identical sha256-verified)
vault-graph-engine.whatDoesNotExist: No .js/.mjs/.ts/.py consuming code anywhere in this directory — no VaultGraph JSON producer, no renderer implementing the spec's rules, no build script, no HTML entry point.
vault-graph-engine.genericBuildingBlockAvailable: graph-engine's hierarchical/radial dagMode layout (wired up this session) is the closest generic, ALREADY-WORKING equivalent of what this spec calls for structurally — a real implementation of that product's specific vault UI (lock overlays, grant edges, tree-view keyboard toggle) remains a downstream, product-specific integration task, deliberately not built here since it's not generic engine capability.

mermaid-engine.purpose: Offline Mermaid diagram rendering — NEW this session (identified as a real gap, researched, built, and verified).
mermaid-engine.verifiedWorking: npm test: 6/6 diagram types render clean (real SVG + ASCII output, non-trivial byte counts checked). Also verified end-to-end through docgen (a real document embedding a Mermaid flowchart, theme-reactive in both dark and light, zero network requests confirmed via browser devtools).

outputFormats: svg (default, CDN font import auto-stripped and replaced with a system-font stack — see README.md)
capabilities.theming: bg/fg accept any CSS color including var(--name) references (with one caveat — see README.md's 'note on the rendered SVG's fonts' and mermaid_bridge.py's docstring: do NOT self-reference the same variable name the library sets locally, use a distinctly-named alias, e.g. docgen's --mermaid-bg/--mermaid-fg pattern in tokens.py).

notImplemented.gantt/gitGraph/mindmap/journey/kanban/pi: Not implemented by the underlying beautiful-mermaid library — a verified, real limit (checked against its own source, not assumed). See tools/mermaid-engine/README.md for what to use instead per type (chart-engine for Gantt/pie, no equivalent yet for mindmap/kanban/etc).

mermaid-engine.whyNotOfficialMermaidOrMermaidCli: Researched and rejected deliberately — see PROVENANCE.md. The official mermaid npm package cannot render to SVG in bare Node (needs real DOM text-measurement); mermaid-cli needs a vendored Chromium (~150-280MB, platform-specific), which would have directly undermined this engine's portability goal far more than a 6-vs-20+ diagram-type scope limit does.

sharedInfrastructure.configuration: engine.config.json + tools/docgen/engine_config.py + tools/lib/engine-config.mjs — see CONFIGURATION.md. Zero required setup; every field has a working default.

projectIndex.implementation: tools/docgen/artifact_index.py (moved here 2026-09-24 — see that module's docstring). tools/project_index/index.py is now a thin re-export shim, kept for this CLI/entryPoint and for any caller already importing tools.project_index.index directly; the move means a host that vendors tools/docgen without also vendoring tools/project_index (because it owns an unrelated package of that name — one downstream host's tools/project_index is its own docs-index gate) no longer breaks tools.docgen.views' audience-view registration.
projectIndex.purpose: A flat JSON registry (PROJECT_INDEX.json) of every document/chart/graph/diagram built for a project, so large-scale work stays navigable — 'what have I already built' instead of losing track. NOT automatic; register artifacts explicitly after creating them worth remembering. `verify` checks the index against the filesystem (missing files, duplicate paths, and — with --scan — built files nothing has claimed), because a hand-maintained map that cannot be falsified stops being worth reading once a project gets large.
projectIndex.verifiedWorking: Registered real artifacts, tested list/search/stats/remove and the HTML dashboard. `verify` added 2026-08-19 and proven by planting a deliberately-stale entry: it reported MISSING and exited 1, where list/stats/dashboard had all displayed the dead entry as a live artifact.
projectIndex.output: PROJECT_INDEX.json (data) + PROJECT_INDEX.html (self-contained dashboard, dark-themed, grouped by section, stat cards by type).

projectCensus.purpose: Measure a project's documentation system from its own git tree (how many documents, updated or outdated, crossed out, stamped as a source of truth and whether the stamps still hold, what is complete per dimension) and its Python code hierarchy; compose them into a report of varied figures (Sankey, stacked bar, heat map, bar, donut, radar, timeline, XY chart, ER diagram, layered diagram) and two explorers (documents, code).
projectCensus.profile: examples/census.profile.example.json (every key optional; unknown keys refused)
projectCensus.verifiedWorking: Measured the engine's own repository and a 1,290-document project in about 7 s; 22 tests against a hand-derived fixture (counts, stamp judgement on the body, rename following, determinism, hostile GIT_DIR, profile refusals, explorer specs, a real docgen build). Building the first report found four defects in other figure kinds (stacked-bar labels, radar labels, layered diagram, Mermaid ER), fixed with red-first tests (OG-292).
projectCensus.limits: Documents are what doc_globs and doc_exts select (Markdown by default); outdated means age, not falsehood; cited means named; no composite completeness number by design.

governance._note: Capabilities that are not figure kinds. Added 2026-08-20 (OG-30): this file claimed to index 'every capability this engine ships' while describing only the rendering surface, so the health system, the build cache and the git moat — three of the engine's four load-bearing subsystems — were invisible to any agent reading it to answer 'what can this engine do'.

health.what: Single fail-closed entry point over five stages: structure, rule layer, cross-file consistency, build, and both npm suites. Exit 0 only when every check that ran PASSED.
health.skip_semantics: A SKIP is unknown, never green. --full and --strict both make a skip fail the run; fast mode tolerates the two mode-gated npm suites and says so explicitly.
health.run_log: .health/runs.jsonl — append-only JSONL, one line per run, on by default

build_cache.what: Content-keyed incremental build over a corpus. Fail-open: any cache problem means a rebuild, never a wrong skip.
key_covers: the out-of-tree renderers (tools/mermaid-engine/, tools/visual-engine/adapters|themes|schemas, and both package-lock.json)

git_moat.install: bash tools/hooks/install.sh  (idempotent; .git/hooks is not version-controlled, so this runs once per checkout)
pre_commit: classification placement over the STAGED index
secret scan over the MATERIALISED staged bytes
pre_push: secret scan over EVERY COMMIT in the pushed range, each materialised into its own directory
classification placement over the same materialised trees
git_moat.known_bypass: git commit --no-verify / git push --no-verify skip every hook silently. No client-side hook can defend against this; see OPEN_GATES OG-31 (Phase 7).
